theme_zh: 班機延誤、錯過轉機時怎麼處理
summary_zh: 學會在機場處理延誤與錯過轉機：改訂、候補、餐券與賠償怎麼說，並用全新的方式重新分清楚現在完成式和過去式。

vocab.definition: a short stop between two flights on the same journey
vocab.example: We have a two-hour layover in Bangkok before the flight to Munich.
vocab.example_zh: 我們飛慕尼黑之前，要在曼谷轉機停留兩小時。

vocab.definition: the second flight you take to continue a journey after changing planes
vocab.example: If the first flight is late, I'll miss my connecting flight.
vocab.example_zh: 如果第一段班機延誤，我就會錯過轉機航班。

vocab.definition: to book a different flight, room, or appointment instead of the original one
vocab.example: The agent rebooked me on the first flight the next morning.
vocab.example_zh: 櫃檯人員幫我改訂隔天早上的第一班飛機。

vocab.definition: waiting to get a seat on a flight that is full, in case someone does not show up
vocab.example: The flight is full, so you're on standby for now.
vocab.example_zh: 這班飛機客滿了，所以你目前是候補。

vocab.definition: a piece of paper or code you can use instead of money for a meal, hotel, or service
vocab.example: They gave us a meal voucher for the airport restaurant.
vocab.example_zh: 他們給我們一張機場餐廳的餐券。

vocab.definition: unable to leave a place, usually because transport is not available
vocab.example: Hundreds of passengers were stranded at the airport after the storm.
vocab.example_zh: 暴風雨過後，好幾百名旅客滯留在機場。

vocab.definition: a small bag you are allowed to take onto the plane with you
vocab.example: I always pack a change of clothes in my carry-on.
vocab.example_zh: 我總是在隨身行李裡放一套換洗衣物。

vocab.definition: money or something else you receive because you have suffered a loss or a problem
vocab.example: You may be able to claim compensation for a long delay.
vocab.example_zh: 班機延誤很久的話，你也許可以申請賠償。

reading.title: A Long Night in Bangkok
paragraphs: Kevin Huang had planned his trip carefully. His flight from Taipei to Munich had a two-hour layover in Bangkok, which looked comfortable at a glance. Then, forty minutes before boarding, the screen above Gate 47 changed from "On time" to "Delayed." A storm had pushed back every departure that evening, and by the time his plane finally took off, Kevin knew he was going to miss his connecting flight.

In Bangkok, the transfer desk was chaos. Dozens of stranded passengers had the same problem, and the two agents on duty were clearly overwhelmed. When Kevin finally reached the front, the agent was calm but honest. "I've rebooked you on the 6 a.m. flight," she said, "but the morning flights have filled up fast, so for now you're on standby." She handed him a hotel voucher and a meal voucher.

Kevin was tired, a little run-down, and had no bandwidth left for anything but sleep. He had come down with a cold the week before, and the dry cabin air had made it flare up again. Luckily, he had packed some over-the-counter cold medicine in his carry-on, so he took two tablets and slept for a few hours at the hotel.

He made the 6 a.m. flight with ten minutes to spare. That was two months ago. Since then, he has flown to Europe three more times, and he hasn't missed a single connection. He has also changed two habits. He never books a short layover anymore, and he always keeps his boarding passes and receipts. A week after that trip, he filed a compensation claim online for the long delay, and the money arrived a month later.

questions.q: Why did Kevin miss his connecting flight?
options: He arrived at the airport in Taipei too late.
A storm delayed his first flight.
The agent in Bangkok made a mistake with his booking.
He fell asleep at the gate in Bangkok.
questions.explain_zh: 第一段寫 A storm had pushed back every departure that evening，因此第一段班機晚起飛，才趕不上轉機。他不是晚到機場，文中也沒說櫃檯人員出錯。

questions.q: What did the agent mean when she said Kevin was "on standby"?
options: He already had a confirmed seat on the 6 a.m. flight.
He had to stay at the hotel until the airline called him.
He would get a seat only if one became available.
He could choose any flight he liked the next day.
questions.explain_zh: 她說 the morning flights have filled up fast, so for now you're on standby：班機已經客滿，所以只是候補，有人沒來才有位子。不是已經確定有位子。

questions.q: What can we infer about Kevin's original two-hour layover?
options: It turned out to be too short to handle a serious delay.
He chose it because it was the cheapest option.
It was longer than the airline usually recommends.
The agent in Bangkok told him to book it.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：第一段說兩小時轉機 looked comfortable at a glance（乍看很充裕），言下之意實際上不夠；最後一段又說他 never books a short layover anymore，可見他認為那次的轉機時間太短。文中沒提到價格或櫃檯建議。

grammar.point_zh: 現在完成式 vs 過去簡單式：說得出「是哪個時間點」用過去式，重點在「到現在」用完成式

guide.key_zh: 先問自己：句子裡有沒有說「何時」？有明確的過去時間就用過去式；沒說何時、或一路延續到現在，就用完成式

uses.label_zh: 過去某個時間點發生、已經結束
uses.signal: last night, at 6 a.m., two months ago, in May
uses.note_zh: 能回答 When? 的句子，幾乎都用過去式

uses.label_zh: 沒說何時，重點是「現在的結果」或「經驗」
uses.note_zh: 美式口語常把 just、already、yet 和過去式連用（I just got my boarding pass.），也是正確的；考試與正式寫作建議用完成式。

uses.label_zh: 從過去一直延續到現在
uses.signal: since then, for three years, so far
uses.note_zh: 中文說「我在這裡從半夜到現在」，英文不能用現在式 I am here since…

mistakes.wrong: I have missed my flight last night.
mistakes.right: I missed my flight last night.
mistakes.why_zh: 有 last night 這種明確的過去時間，只能用過去式

mistakes.wrong: I am at this airport since midnight.
mistakes.right: I have been at this airport since midnight.
mistakes.why_zh: since 表示「到現在」，要用完成式，不能用現在式

mistakes.wrong: Ticket prices have been gone up since May.
mistakes.right: Ticket prices have gone up since May.
mistakes.why_zh: go 是不及物動詞，沒有被動；have been gone 只用在「離開多久了」（He's been gone for an hour）。「價格上漲」只要 have gone up

timeline.label: My flight left Taipei three hours late last night.
I've just gotten my new boarding pass.
I've been at this airport since midnight.

examples.en: We landed in Bangkok at 11:40 last night.
examples.zh: 我們昨晚 11:40 降落曼谷。（明確的時間點→過去式）

examples.en: I've already rebooked you on the morning flight.
examples.zh: 我已經幫你改訂早上的班機了。（沒說何時，重點是現在已經訂好）

examples.en: She has worked for the airline since 2019.
examples.zh: 她從 2019 年起就在這家航空公司工作。（一直延續到現在）

exercises.q: My flight ___ (leave) Taipei three hours late last night.
exercises.explain_zh: last night 是明確的過去時間，事情已經結束 → 過去式 left。不能說 has left last night。

exercises.q: So far, the airline ___ (cancel) four flights because of the storm.
exercises.explain_zh: so far（到目前為止）表示從過去累積到現在 → 現在完成式。主詞 the airline 是單數，用 has。美式拼 canceled、英式拼 cancelled，都可以。

exercises.q: I ___ (be) at this airport since midnight, and I'm exhausted.
exercises.explain_zh: since midnight 表示從半夜一直到現在 → have been。中文「我從半夜就在這裡」沒有時態變化，但英文不能說 I am here since midnight。

exercises.q: Ticket prices ___ (go) up a lot since last summer.
exercises.explain_zh: since last summer → 現在完成式，主詞 prices 是複數，用 have gone；強調一路持續上漲也可以說 have been going up。注意不要寫成 have been gone：go 是不及物動詞，沒有被動，have been gone 只用在「離開多久了」（He's been gone for an hour）。

options: have you got
have you gotten
did you get
you got
exercises.explain_zh: When 問的是「哪個時間點」，答案一定是過去的某個時刻 → 過去式 did you get。現在完成式不能和 When 問句連用；you got 少了助動詞 did，是問句語序錯誤。

options: I've missed my connecting flight yesterday.
I've been missed my connecting flight yesterday.
I was miss my connecting flight yesterday.
I missed my connecting flight yesterday.
exercises.explain_zh: yesterday 是明確的過去時間 → 過去式 I missed。have missed 不能接 yesterday；have been missed 是被動，意思和形式都不對；was miss 混用了 be 動詞和原形。

review.point: Present perfect continuous for ongoing situations
review.point_zh: 現在完成進行式：從過去開始、到現在還在持續的狀況（have/has been + V-ing）

exercises.q: My throat ___ (hurt) since we boarded the plane.
exercises.explain_zh: 從登機開始痛、到現在還在痛 → has been hurting（been 後面接 V-ing）。不要寫成 has been hurt：have/has been + 過去分詞是被動（被傷害），意思完全不同。主詞 my throat 是單數，用 has。

exercises.q: I ___ (try) to call the airline for an hour, but nobody is picking up.
exercises.explain_zh: 從一小時前開始打、到現在還在打 → 現在完成進行式 have been trying（been 後面接 V-ing）。for an hour 表示持續多久，而且動作還沒結束，所以不用過去式 tried。注意不要寫成 have been tried：have been + 過去分詞是被動（被嘗試），意思不對。主詞是 I，用 have。

exercises.q: We ___ in this line for forty minutes, and it still isn't moving.
options: have been standing
have been stood
stood
are standing
exercises.explain_zh: for forty minutes 到現在還在排 → have been standing（been + V-ing）。have been stood 是「被動＋過去分詞」的錯誤組合；stood 表示已經結束；are standing 不能搭配 for forty minutes 表示持續多久。

guide.key_zh: 從過去開始、到現在還在持續的事，用 have/has been + V-ing

uses.label_zh: 從過去一直持續到現在（還在進行）
uses.signal: for two weeks, since August, lately, all day

uses.label_zh: 看到現在的樣子，推測剛剛一直在做什麼

mistakes.wrong: I've been seeing three apartments this week.
mistakes.right: I've seen three apartments this week.
mistakes.why_zh: 講次數、結果用現在完成式，不用進行式

mistakes.wrong: I've been knowing him for years.
mistakes.why_zh: know、like、own 這類狀態動詞通常不用進行式

mistakes.wrong: I've been working here since three years.
mistakes.right: I've been working here for three years.
mistakes.why_zh: for 接一段時間，since 接開始的時間點

timeline.label: I've been looking for an apartment since August.
I saw one yesterday.
timeline.note_zh: 對照：過去式，一個時間點

listening.title: At the Transfer Desk

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Hi. My flight from Taipei landed late, and I've missed my connecting flight to Munich.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Nadia
lines.text: I'm sorry about that. Can I see your boarding pass? Okay, yes, the storm pushed back a lot of departures tonight.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Is there another flight to Munich tonight?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Nadia
lines.text: I'm afraid the last one left at 11:15. I've put you on the 6 a.m. flight, but it's full at the moment, so you're on standby.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Standby? So I might not get on?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Nadia
lines.text: There's a good chance you will. People often don't show up for early flights. If you don't get a seat, I'll rebook you on the 1 p.m. flight, which has plenty of space.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Okay. And will the miles from my original booking carry over to the new one?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Nadia
lines.text: Yes, they'll carry over automatically. Your checked bag will be transferred too, so you only need your carry-on tonight. Here's a hotel voucher and a meal voucher.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Thanks. One more thing: can I still ask for compensation for the delay?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Nadia
lines.text: Yes, you can file a claim online after your trip. Just keep your boarding passes and receipts.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Great. Thanks for your help, Nadia. It's been a long night.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Nadia
lines.text: I bet. Get some rest, and good luck in the morning.

questions.q: Why can't Kevin fly to Munich tonight?
options: The airline has canceled all flights because of the storm.
The last flight to Munich has already left.
His checked bag hasn't arrived yet.
He doesn't have a valid boarding pass.
questions.explain_zh: Nadia 說 I'm afraid the last one left at 11:15：今晚最後一班已經飛走了。她沒說所有班機都取消，行李也會自動轉運。

questions.q: What will happen if Kevin doesn't get a seat on the 6 a.m. flight?
options: He will get a full refund.
He will have to buy a new ticket.
He will stay another night at the hotel.
He will be rebooked on the 1 p.m. flight.
questions.explain_zh: Nadia 說 If you don't get a seat, I'll rebook you on the 1 p.m. flight：候補不到就改訂下午一點那班。

questions.q: Why does Nadia mention that people often don't show up for early flights?
options: To tell Kevin he will probably get a seat.
To warn Kevin that the 6 a.m. flight might be canceled.
To suggest that Kevin take a later flight instead.
To explain why the airline overbooks morning flights.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：Kevin 擔心 So I might not get on?，Nadia 回 There's a good chance you will，接著說早班常有人沒來，意思是會空出位子，他很可能上得了飛機。

dictation: I've missed my connecting flight to Munich.
I've put you on the 6 a.m. flight, but it's full at the moment, so you're on standby.
Just keep your boarding passes and receipts.

shadowing: I've missed my connecting flight to Munich.
The last flight left at 11:15, so I've put you on the morning one.
I've been at this airport since midnight.
Can I still ask for compensation for the delay?

prompts.question: Read this line from the dialogue aloud twice: "I've put you on the 6 a.m. flight, but it's full at the moment, so you're on standby."
prompts.question_zh: 把對話中的這句唸兩次（一分鐘內就能完成）：注意 I've、it's、you're 的縮寫要唸得連起來。
prompts.sample: I've put you on the 6 a.m. flight, but it's full at the moment, so you're on standby.

prompts.question: Have you ever had a flight delayed or canceled? Say when it happened, what you did, and what you've done differently since then.
prompts.question_zh: 你有沒有遇過班機延誤或取消？說說是什麼時候、你當時怎麼處理，以及從那之後你有什麼改變。
prompts.sample: Yes, I've had a few delays, but the worst one was in 2023. I was flying to Tokyo for work, and the flight was delayed by six hours because of a typhoon. I waited at the gate, got a sandwich with a meal voucher, and called my client to push back our meeting. Since then, I've always booked an earlier flight whenever I have something important the next day.

writing.task: Your first flight was delayed and you missed your connecting flight. Write an email of 80-150 words to the airline's customer service. Use three short paragraphs: (1) the situation — what happened and when; (2) what you tried — what the airport staff did for you; (3) the next step — what you would like the airline to do now. Tip: don't join two full sentences with just a comma. Use a period, or a comma plus a joining word such as and, but, or so.
writing.task_zh: 你的第一段班機延誤，錯過了轉機。寫一封 80–150 個英文字的 email 給航空公司客服，分三小段：(1) 狀況：發生什麼事、什麼時候；(2) 你試過什麼：機場人員怎麼幫你處理；(3) 下一步：你希望航空公司現在做什麼。小提醒：兩個完整句子不能只用逗號連起來：用句號，或用逗號加 and／but／so 等連接詞。
writing.sample:
Dear Customer Service,

I am writing about my trip from Taipei to Munich on November 2. My first flight left Taipei three hours late because of a storm, so I missed my connecting flight in Bangkok.

The agent at the transfer desk rebooked me on the 6 a.m. flight the next morning. She also gave me a hotel voucher. I was on standby, but luckily I got a seat.

I arrived in Munich nine hours later than planned. I have kept all my boarding passes and receipts, and I have attached them to this email. I have not heard from the airline since I got back, and I believe I am eligible for compensation for the delay. Could you please let me know the next steps?

Best regards,
Kevin Huang
checklist_zh: 分三段：發生什麼事（何時）→ 機場人員怎麼處理 → 希望航空公司接下來做什麼
有明確時間（on November 2、the next morning）用過去式；到現在的結果用 have/has + 過去分詞（I have attached…）
兩個完整句子不能只用逗號連起來：用句號，或用逗號加 and／but／so 等連接詞
用到 connecting flight、rebook、since、compensation，總長 80–150 字

translation.zh: 自從我們推出新方案以來，註冊人數已經成長了 18%。
translation.en: Sign-ups have grown by 18% since we launched the new plan.
alt: Sign-ups have increased by 18% since we launched the new plan.
Sign-ups have gone up by 18% since we launched the new plan.

translation.zh: 我的班機昨晚延誤了三個小時。
translation.en: My flight was delayed by three hours last night.
alt: My flight was three hours late last night.
Last night, my flight was delayed by three hours.
My flight was delayed for three hours last night.

translation.zh: 到目前為止，我已經改訂了兩次機票。
translation.en: So far, I've rebooked my flight twice.
alt: So far, I have rebooked my flight twice.
I've rebooked my flight twice so far.
I have rebooked my flight twice so far.

reading.title: The Overbooking Game
paragraphs: Anyone who flies regularly has heard the announcement: "This flight is oversold, and we're looking for volunteers willing to take a later flight." To many passengers, it sounds as if the airline has messed up. In reality, it is usually the result of a carefully calculated bet.

Airlines know that on any given route, a certain share of ticket holders will not turn up. Some miss connections, some change their plans at the last minute, and some business travelers book two flights and only take one. Rather than fly with empty seats, carriers sell more tickets than the plane can hold, using years of data to predict how many no-shows to expect. Most of the time, the numbers work out and nobody notices.

When they don't, the airline first asks for volunteers, and this is where seasoned travelers see an opportunity. The opening offer is often modest: a meal voucher and a seat on the next departure. Frequent flyers know that the offer tends to go up if nobody bites, so they hang back and wait. On a busy holiday weekend, a patient passenger can walk away with a travel credit worth several hundred dollars, sometimes with an upgrade thrown in.

Being bumped against your will is a different story. Rules vary from country to country, but in many places an airline must compensate passengers it denies boarding involuntarily, and the amount usually rises with the length of the delay. Still, few people know their rights, and not every gate agent will spell out the details unprompted.

The lesson for travelers is simple. If your plans are flexible, an oversold flight may be the best deal you'll get all year. If they aren't, check in early: passengers who check in last are often the first to be bumped.

questions.q: Why do airlines sell more tickets than there are seats?
options: They expect some passengers not to turn up.
They want to force passengers to buy upgrades.
Their booking systems often make mistakes.
They are required to keep a few seats for staff.
questions.explain_zh: 第二段：a certain share of ticket holders will not turn up… Rather than fly with empty seats, carriers sell more tickets：航空公司預期會有人沒來，不想空位飛，才超賣。

questions.q: Why do frequent flyers "hang back" when the first offer is announced?
options: They don't want to miss their own meetings.
They hope the airline will raise the offer if no one accepts.
They know volunteers are rarely chosen.
They are waiting to be bumped involuntarily.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：文中說 the offer tends to go up if nobody bites, so they hang back and wait——常飛的人知道沒人接受時補償會加碼，所以先按兵不動。

questions.q: What does the writer suggest about passengers who are bumped involuntarily?
options: They usually receive more than the volunteers do.
Airlines almost never have to pay them anything.
Many may not get everything they are entitled to, because they don't know their rights.
Most of them are business travelers who booked two flights.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：第四段說 few people know their rights, and not every gate agent will spell out the details unprompted——多數人不知道自己的權益，櫃檯也不一定主動說明，暗示他們可能拿不到應得的賠償。文中說的是航空公司 must compensate，所以「幾乎不用付錢」不對。

listening.title: Volunteering at the Gate

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Excuse me, sir, are you the one who asked about volunteering? We're still oversold by two.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Yeah, that was me. So, um, what exactly are you offering?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Right now it's a seat on the 9:40 tomorrow morning, a hotel near the airport, and a two-hundred-dollar travel credit.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Two hundred. Hmm. The thing is, I've got a meeting in Munich on Monday, so I'd be cutting it pretty close—

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: You'd land Sunday night, so you'd still make it. Honestly, it's a pretty good offer.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Sure, but— okay, could you upgrade me to business on the new flight?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: I can't promise that. What I can do is put you at the top of the upgrade list.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Okay. And if nobody else volunteers, does the credit go up?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Well, it might. But if I end up having to bump people, the offer's off the table. I'd have to go by check-in order, starting with whoever checked in last.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Ah, got it. So it's now or never, basically.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Pretty much. Should I go ahead and rebook you?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Yeah, go ahead. Just make sure my bag comes off this flight, okay?

questions.q: Why does Kevin hesitate at first?
options: He thinks the hotel is too far from the airport.
He doesn't want to lose his checked bag.
He has already used his travel credit.
He's worried about getting to his meeting on time.
questions.explain_zh: Kevin 說 I've got a meeting in Munich on Monday, so I'd be cutting it pretty close：他擔心時間太趕，來不及開會。

questions.q: What does Priya offer instead of a guaranteed upgrade?
options: A bigger travel credit.
A place at the top of the upgrade list.
A seat on an earlier flight.
A free meal at the hotel.
questions.explain_zh: Priya 說 I can't promise that. What I can do is put you at the top of the upgrade list：無法保證升等，但可以把他排在升等名單第一位。

questions.q: Why does Kevin agree quickly at the end?
options: Priya has already raised the travel credit.
He has decided he doesn't need to go to the meeting.
He realizes that the offer could disappear if he waits.
